full_cake_replacement.description: Replaces the NVIDIA stack end-to-end. Examples: AMD Helios, hyperscaler custom silicon (where applicable).

fabric_alternatives.description: Replaces ONLY the fabric layer within the cake. The rest of the NVIDIA stack remains.

software_alternatives.description: Replaces ONLY the software wrapper / programming-stack layer. The rest of the NVIDIA stack (GPU + fabric + OEM + ISV) remains. Currently: NVIDIA NVAIE (CUDA-rooted) vs AMD ROCm. Phase 3c-2 step 2 will render this as a software-layer scorecard extending the AMD full-stack-replacement view.

uec_coalition.description: Ultra Ethernet Consortium members — open-standard fabric coalition. Includes AMD, Cornelis, Broadcom, hyperscalers. Broadcom designs hyperscaler chips, making them a double enabler.

provenance.source: Ultra Ethernet Consortium public member roster.

paradigm_alternative.description: Architecturally different machines that do NOT decompose into NVIDIA's L1-L5 layer model. Adopting them is a re-architecture, not a stack swap. Currently: Cerebras WSE-3 (wafer-scale inference appliance). Rendered via the layer-fight-map PARADIGM state across all bands + a cross-layer ParadigmContrast explainer panel.

customer_self_supply.description: NVIDIA's biggest customers becoming their own suppliers via vertical integration. Strategic-context entries — NOT layer-fight-map competitors (most chips are internal / captive and not publicly benchmarked vs NVIDIA spec-for-spec; forcing them onto the cake would mis-frame a market-structure threat as a spec fight). Differentiated by MATURITY; the spread across the 4 is the insight (NOT a monolith). Currently: Google TPU v7 Ironwood (most mature + only merchant) / AWS Trainium3 (commercial volume + NVLink Fusion coexistence) / Meta MTIA (narrow + internal) / Microsoft Maia 200 (least mature + OpenAI-volume-justified). Rendered via the HyperscalerSelfSupplyView strategic panel (header framing + 4 maturity-differentiated cards + 5-facet calibrated verdict). On the switching-cost spectrum: this is the buyer-exits-the-market end.

components.name: AMD ROCm (CUDA-equivalent software stack)
components.positioning: AMD's CUDA-equivalent open-source software stack. Runs on AMD Instinct (MI300X / MI355X / MI455X). ROCm 7.x is the current generation (recent releases through ROCm 7.2.x per AMD ROCm release docs). Mainstream PyTorch / vLLM / SGLang inference path is viable today; the moat that remains is CUDA's library exclusivity (TensorRT-LLM, FlashAttention 3) and ~20-year ecosystem depth. Paired with amd_mi355x (current GPU) for the full-stack-replacement competitive view.
components.moat_framing: ROCm has made real progress on mainstream inference — PyTorch + vLLM + SGLang all have official ROCm support, and MI300X/MI355X are competitive with H100/B200 on memory-bound workloads. The remaining gap is precise: (1) CUDA-exclusive libraries (TensorRT-LLM, FlashAttention 3) with no full ROCm equivalent — missing FA3 reportedly costs 30-40% training throughput on 7B+ models per Spheron May 2026; (2) CUDA's ~20-year ecosystem depth (cuDNN, cuBLAS, TensorRT, NCCL); (3) CUDA-first default for new research and tooling. The switching cost is high but workload-dependent — viable for mainstream PyTorch/vLLM workflows, costly for CUDA-native codebases with exclusive-lib dependencies. NEVER claim ROCm parity with CUDA; NEVER claim ROCm broken — the honest read is 'depends what you're building.'

software_framework_support.text: PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang official ROCm support (ROCm 7.x current generation; PyTorch ships ROCm-native paths; vLLM has official ROCm support with AMD Zen CPU backend + RDNA 3.5/4 device IDs; SGLang inference performance testing documented on ROCm). Additional: FlashInfer, llama.cpp. Training frameworks: Megatron-LM, verl.

provenance.source: AMD ROCm Compatibility Matrix + ROCm 7.x release notes + vLLM official ROCm path + SGLang inference docs on ROCm. Cross-confirmed across AMD docs + framework release notes.
provenance.notes: Official support across major ML frameworks is verified across multiple sources. Specific 'ROCm 7.2 / Jan 2026' release timing not independently confirmed in web search; ROCm 7.x is the current generation per AMD docs (releases through 7.2.x referenced).

software_mainstream_inference.text: Workload-dependent. Memory-bound inference: MI300X often beats H100 (~40% lower latency on Llama-2-70B per Clarifai / Tensorwave 2026 benchmarks). Compute-bound: H100 leads (vLLM ROCm latency 37-75% higher than H200 in some configurations per aimultiple 2026). The optimistic '~90-95% of H100 throughput' framing applies to specific PyTorch/vLLM workloads but does not cleanly verify as a single number.

provenance.source: Independent benchmarks split by workload type. Clarifai + Tensorwave + SemiAnalysis 2026 coverage shows MI300X memory-bound wins (Llama-2-70B ~40% lower latency, Llama3 405B + DeepSeekv3 670B absolute + per-dollar wins). aimultiple 2026 + ROCm vLLM docs show vLLM ROCm-vs-CUDA latency gap on compute-bound (MI300X 37-75% higher latency than H200 in tested configurations).
provenance.notes: WORKLOAD-DEPENDENT — not directly comparable as a single number. Memory-bound MI300X often wins; compute-bound H100 leads. Software stack maturity gap between vLLM ROCm vs CUDA is the structural variable. The '~90-95%' figure originates in optimistic vendor + early-benchmark framing; conservative independent reads show wider variance. Pill flagged VERIFY-NEEDED to reflect this. Honest read: 'competitive on mainstream PyTorch / vLLM inference, workload-dependent — neither vendor cleanly wins across the board.'

software_cuda_exclusive_libs.text: Gap, not strength: TensorRT-LLM (NVIDIA-only, no ROCm equivalent — confirmed AMD ROCm docs + Spheron 2026 + Thundercompute 2026); FlashAttention 3 (CUDA-only as of 2026 — AMD has FlashAttention 2 via Triton for RDNA3 since ROCm 6.4 March 2025, but FA3 port incomplete; missing FA3 costs 30-40% training throughput on 7B+ models per Spheron May 2026); NCCL collective comm (no ROCm equivalent). This is the precise library moat ROCm has NOT closed.

provenance.source: Multiple 2026 analyses confirm: TensorRT-LLM is CUDA-only by design with no ROCm port (Spheron, SemiAnalysis, Thundercompute 2026 comparisons). FlashAttention 3 ROCm port incomplete — AMD PyTorch compatibility docs acknowledge FA3 integration but practitioners report FA3 gap costs 30-40% training throughput on 7B+ models (Spheron May 2026 quantification).
provenance.notes: The library moat is real, specific, and NAMED. Not 'ROCm is broken' — it's 'ROCm doesn't have THESE specific libraries.' Workloads using TensorRT-LLM or FA3 should stay on CUDA; workloads on stock PyTorch / vLLM can move with variable performance cost.

software_ecosystem_maturity.text: ROCm is closing the depth gap (ROCm 7.x release cadence + framework integration progress) but is not at CUDA parity. CUDA has ~20 years of compounding ecosystem (released 2007); ROCm has been on the modern AI-targeted cadence for roughly half that. Library breadth (cuDNN / cuBLAS / TensorRT / NCCL) and CUDA-first tooling default remain the structural moat.

provenance.source: Comparative ecosystem-maturity characterization synthesized from CUDA release timeline + practitioner survey coverage + analyst reports (Spheron 2026, Thundercompute 2026). Directional — no single measured KPI captures 'ecosystem maturity.'

software_switching_cost.text: High but workload-dependent. CUDA-native codebases (especially those depending on TensorRT-LLM, FlashAttention 3, or NCCL) require significant port effort + performance acceptance penalty. Codebases already abstracted (PyTorch + vLLM + SGLang) port with less friction — these frameworks have official ROCm paths. CUDA-first tooling default for new research/work perpetuates the asymmetry.

provenance.source: Switching cost characterization synthesized from practitioner reports of CUDA -> ROCm porting efforts + analyst coverage (Spheron 2026, Thundercompute 2026). The high/workload-dependent split is the structurally honest read.

components.name: AMD Instinct MI355X (CDNA 4, current shipping)
components.positioning: Current-shipping AMD AI accelerator (launched 12 June 2025, CDNA 4 / 3nm / 185B transistors, 1400W TBP liquid-cooled). The honest current-generation contemporary of NVIDIA Blackwell B200 — both shipping today, hardware close to parity. AMD's 2026 roadmap successor is Helios MI455X (separate component, generation: roadmap).
components.moat_framing: Hardware is near-parity with B200 (memory capacity leads, bandwidth ties, FP4 essentially even, FP8 close). AMD's gap is ROCm vs CUDA — ROCm has been closing the gap but is not at parity, and TensorRT-LLM remains NVIDIA-only and won't run on ROCm. The moat conversation has moved from silicon to software; the 2026 generation (MI455X) extends the spec lead but does not bridge the ROCm-vs-CUDA gap.

provenance.source: AMD Instinct MI355X product page + datasheet brief — 288 GB HBM3e per GPU, 4th Gen CDNA architecture. Confirmed across multiple sources (AMD product page, Wikipedia AMD Instinct table, Oracle OCI deployment blog, Flopper.io spec sheet).
provenance.notes: Per-GPU figure — 50% larger than Blackwell B200 (192 GB). Vendor-claimed (AMD source materials); pill renders CLAIMED. Both products are shipping today (MI355X launched 12 June 2025) — the CITED-vs-CLAIMED distinction reflects evidence basis (NVIDIA datasheet-confirmed vs AMD vendor-stated), NOT announced-vs-shipping.

provenance.source: AMD Instinct MI355X product brief — 8 TB/s memory bandwidth (HBM3e). Multiple sources confirm (AMD product page, Wikipedia, Flopper.io).
provenance.notes: At parity with B200's 8 TB/s. Vendor-claimed (AMD source materials); both shipping today. The CITED-vs-CLAIMED pill split reflects evidence basis only.

Consistent with Wikipedia's reported 20.1 PFLOPS FP4 (with sparsity) / 2x dense:sparse ratio = ~10 PFLOPS dense. Vendor figure-spread is within ~10% noise — 9.2 is the AMD-cited dense number.
provenance.notes: DENSE / SPARSE caveat applies — AMD has not always explicitly stated dense vs sparse split in announcement materials; figure may not be apples-to-apples with NVIDIA B200's explicit dense/sparse split (9 PFLOPS dense / 18 PFLOPS sparse). Comparison vs B200's 9 PFLOPS FP4 dense is near-parity (~9.2 vs ~9, within ~2% — clean PARITY for the scorecard's ~5% tolerance). The parity finding holds regardless of small vendor-claim variance.

provenance.source: Tom's Hardware ISSCC 2026 article reports MI355X at 'five petaflops of FP8 compute, a 1.9x improvement over MI300X' (per-CU FP8 throughput doubled from 4,096 to 8,192 FLOPS/clock — implied dense matrix figure). Other published figures vary widely: Flopper.io lists 10.1 PFLOPS FP8; AMD platform materials cite 40.3 PFLOPS FP8 matrix dense and 80.5 PFLOPS with sparsity — these likely measure different scopes (per-GPU matrix vs scalar, OCP-FP8 vs general FP8).
provenance.notes: DENSE/SPARSE caveat applies (AMD has not explicitly stated; figures depend on measurement methodology). Figure-spread across sources (5, 10.1, 40.3, 80.5 PFLOPS) reflects different measurement scopes — flagged VERIFY-NEEDED in addition to CLAIMED until reconciled against AMD's authoritative datasheet. Comparison vs B200's 9 PFLOPS FP8 dense (itself verify-needed) — BOTH sides low-confidence on this axis, scorecard renders UNRESOLVED rather than a winner.

components.name: Broadcom Tomahawk Ultra (Ethernet for AI scale-up)
components.positioning: Within-cake fabric swap. Tomahawk Ultra is Broadcom's AI-optimized merchant Ethernet switch chip (announced + shipping mid-2025) — 51.2 Tbps total switch capacity, 64x 800GbE ports, 250 ns port-to-port latency, 77 billion PPS. Pin-compatible with Tomahawk 5 for fast OEM time-to-market. Broadcom also designs hyperscaler custom AI chips and supplies the Jericho3-AI silicon inside Arista 7800R4/7700R4 — making Broadcom a double enabler (fabric chip + ODM silicon).

Demo-narration framing: TRANSPARENCY, NOT NECESSARILY SUPERIORITY — head-to-head latency comparison favors Broadcom's evidence base over vendors whose per-hop latency is unpublished, but a missing number from NVIDIA/Cornelis is NOT evidence of worse performance. The honest read is 'Broadcom is the only one publishing the number,' not 'Broadcom is the fastest.'

components.name: Cerebras WSE-3 (wafer-scale inference appliance)
components.positioning: ALTERNATIVE PARADIGM. Cerebras does NOT decompose into NVIDIA's L1-L5 layer model — the WSE-3 is a single wafer with 900,000 cores, 4T transistors, 44GB on-chip SRAM, and ~21 PB/s on-chip bandwidth, packaged in the CS-3 appliance (~23 kW). The architectural thesis: by eliminating inter-chip communication entirely, the wafer removes the multi-GPU-cluster bottleneck that bounds NVIDIA distributed-GPU collective performance. Adopting Cerebras is a re-architecture, not a slot-swap. Public + validated (IPO May 2026, OpenAI 750 MW / $10-20B multi-year, AWS Bedrock Mar 2026) but narrow in workload-fit (inference-specific, Llama-class reasoning sweet spot) and small relative to NVIDIA (NVIDIA ~90% accelerator share, ~423× Cerebras revenue).
components.moat_framing: Cerebras is the cleanest PARADIGM-state case in the demo: respect the architecture (real, novel, validated at the public-market level), size the scale honestly (fast-growing sliver, not imminent displacement), and locate NVIDIA's moat in the layers Cerebras structurally cannot fill — breadth, full training+inference range, the CUDA/NVAIE ecosystem, and the flexibility to deploy across the full workload spectrum. The 3-facet verdict (SERIOUS-BUT-NARROW + NICHE-SHARP + MARKET-ARC) all three must hold simultaneously — cherry-picking 'serious' alone would inflate the threat; cherry-picking 'niche' alone would dismiss real validation. The honest read is calibrated: precision strike on a specific inference niche, not a stack swap.

paradigm_wafer_architecture.text: 900,000 cores · 4 trillion transistors · 125 PF peak · 44 GB on-chip SRAM · ~21 PB/s on-chip bandwidth (~2,625× NVIDIA B200) · CS-3 appliance ~23 kW · NO inter-chip communication latency (the multi-GPU-cluster bottleneck — eliminated by the monolithic-wafer architecture)

provenance.source: Cerebras WSE-3 product specifications + CS-3 appliance datasheet, corroborated by independent semiconductor analyst coverage (SemiAnalysis, AnandTech, Tom's Hardware). The ~2,625× bandwidth comparison vs B200 is structurally derived from published per-component bandwidth figures.
provenance.notes: Architecture facts are CITED + structurally verifiable (transistor count, core count, on-chip memory, on-chip bandwidth) — the no-inter-chip-latency thesis is the architecturally real consequence of the wafer-scale design.

paradigm_inference_claims.text: Up to 21× faster than NVIDIA DGX B200 on Llama 3 70B reasoning (specific token configuration) · ~32% lower TCO on the same workload · Meta Llama API integration showing 18× inference speedup · OpenAI deployments at 1,000+ tokens/sec

NOT a general speedup. NEVER render as 'Cerebras is 21× faster' flat. Workload-fit + benchmark-scope caveats are mandatory framing — without them, the claim overreaches.

provenance.source: Google Cloud TPU availability + Meta-in-talks coverage (Reuters, The Information, CNBC 2026) + Gemini 3 training disclosure (Google announcements).

self_supply_coexistence_signal.text: Most direct self-supply-becomes-competitor path of the 4. Customers picking TPU outside GCP move workloads off NVIDIA more decisively than other hyperscaler chips. BUT: frontier model partnerships across the industry still flow through NVIDIA for cross-vendor compatibility; Google itself still buys NVIDIA for many GCP workloads.

provenance.source: Industry analyst coverage of TPU merchant deployments + Google Cloud's continued NVIDIA H100 / B200 availability for customers who require it.
provenance.notes: Coexistence is real even for the merchant-threat case — Google sells both TPU and NVIDIA capacity on GCP; the threat is in customer-share trajectory, not zero-sum replacement.

components.name: AWS Trainium3
components.positioning: COMMERCIAL VOLUME + the MOST EXPLICIT COEXISTENCE signal. Trainium3 went GA December 2025 (3nm, 2.52 PFLOPS FP8) and is anchored by Anthropic + OpenAI workloads driving AWS volume. The defining coexistence signal: Trainium4 integrates NVLink Fusion (AWS-NVIDIA collaboration) — AWS is NOT trying to replace NVIDIA wholesale; the partnership says 'self-supply specific workloads + NVIDIA stays for the rest.' This is the not-zero-sum case in its purest form across the 4.

self_supply_maturity_tier.text: COMMERCIAL VOLUME + COEXISTENCE — anchored by Anthropic + OpenAI for volume; coexists explicitly with NVIDIA via NVLink Fusion in Trainium4

provenance.source: AWS re:Invent 2025 Trainium3 GA announcement + Anthropic / OpenAI Trainium adoption coverage + AWS-NVIDIA NVLink Fusion partnership announcement (re:Invent 2025).

self_supply_chip_specs.text: GA December 2025 · 3nm process · 2.52 PFLOPS FP8 · anchored by Anthropic + OpenAI workloads on AWS

provenance.source: AWS Trainium3 specifications (AWS re:Invent 2025) + Anthropic + OpenAI Trainium adoption (AWS press releases, customer case studies).
provenance.notes: Public AWS-published specs. NOT independently benchmarked vs NVIDIA B200 spec-for-spec — workload-specific deployment, not spec comparison.

self_supply_deployment_state.text: GA on AWS only (captive cloud — NOT merchant; you can rent Trainium3 capacity on AWS, but Trainium3 chips do not ship outside AWS). Anthropic + OpenAI workloads driving production volume.

provenance.source: AWS Trainium3 availability is AWS-cloud-only by design (AWS Trainium product positioning).

self_supply_coexistence_signal.text: Trainium4 integrates NVLink Fusion (AWS-NVIDIA collaboration announced re:Invent 2025) — the most explicit coexistence signal across the 4 hyperscaler programs. AWS is NOT trying to replace NVIDIA wholesale; the partnership says 'self-supply specific workloads + NVIDIA stays for the rest.' AWS continues to sell NVIDIA H100 / B200 / GB200 capacity at scale.

provenance.source: AWS-NVIDIA NVLink Fusion partnership announcement (AWS re:Invent 2025 + NVIDIA GTC announcements) + AWS continued NVIDIA capacity (P5 / P5e instance families).

components.name: Meta MTIA (gens 300 / 400 / 500)
components.positioning: NARROW + INTERNAL — 100,000s of units deployed inside Meta (Facebook + Instagram inference workloads); NOT sold externally. RISC-V architecture, gens 300 / 400 / 500 in production. The defining limit-of-own-program signal: Meta is in talks to license or buy Google TPUs (billions, reported) — Meta hedges across NVIDIA + MTIA + (potentially) TPU. NOT 'Meta replaces NVIDIA with MTIA'; it's 'multi-vendor diversification.' Meta still buys NVIDIA for frontier training at scale.

self_supply_maturity_tier.text: NARROW + INTERNAL — 100,000s deployed but production-only-inside-Meta, no external availability; Meta in talks for Google TPUs (limits-of-own-program signal)

provenance.source: Meta MTIA deployment scale (Meta engineering blog + analyst coverage); Meta-in-talks-for-Google-TPUs coverage (Reuters, The Information 2026).

self_supply_chip_specs.text: MTIA generations 300 / 400 / 500 · RISC-V architecture · 100,000s of units deployed in Meta production (FB + IG inference)

provenance.source: Meta engineering blog + RISC-V Foundation announcements + semiconductor-analyst coverage of MTIA generations.
provenance.notes: MTIA is internal-only by design — no public spec-vs-NVIDIA benchmarks exist. Architecture facts are CITED via Meta disclosures.

self_supply_deployment_state.text: Internal-only. 100,000s of MTIA units in Meta production for FB + IG inference workloads. NOT for sale externally. Meta uses NVIDIA for frontier training + MTIA for specific inference workloads — coexistence within Meta is multi-vendor by design.

provenance.source: Meta engineering blog disclosures + analyst coverage of Meta's multi-vendor AI infrastructure strategy.

self_supply_coexistence_signal.text: Multi-vendor pattern within Meta. NVIDIA for training + MTIA for inference; reportedly exploring TPU adoption (billions, in talks) — Meta hedges across multiple silicon vendors, not replacing NVIDIA with MTIA. The Meta-in-talks-for-TPU signal explicitly bounds MTIA's own-program reach.

provenance.source: Meta multi-vendor infrastructure strategy coverage + Meta-in-talks-for-Google-TPUs reporting (Reuters, The Information 2026).
provenance.notes: Coexistence is real AND the in-talks-for-TPU signal shows the limits of any single self-supply program — even Meta hedges.

components.name: Microsoft Maia 200
components.positioning: LEAST MATURE — earliest of the 4 self-supply programs. Maia 200 (3nm, 216 GB HBM3e, vendor-claimed ~3× Trainium3 FP4 — claimed, not independently benchmarked) is ramping; OpenAI's Azure compute volume justifies the program economically. OpenAI continues to use NVIDIA + AWS Trainium in parallel — Microsoft hasn't replaced NVIDIA volume; Maia adds capacity for OpenAI-specific workloads. Earliest of the 4, not the most concerning to NVIDIA today.

self_supply_maturity_tier.text: LEAST MATURE — earliest of the 4 programs; OpenAI's Azure compute volume is what justifies Maia economically (anchor-customer-driven, not broad-platform)

provenance.source: Microsoft Ignite 2025 Maia 200 announcement + OpenAI Azure compute volume coverage + semiconductor-analyst comparisons across the 4 hyperscaler programs.
